subject: Secure key escrow, EKM proxy and TLS interoperability — clarifications
messages:
From: Jacob Liao <jacob.liao@medicorp.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: security@medicorp.com
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Questions: BYOK/brokered escrow paths + TLS cipher profile

Rishi,

Thanks for the quick intro yesterday. As part of our procurement RFP we've got a short list of technical clarifications before we move to an on-site (virtual) architecture review. Can you confirm the following for Redwood's private and dedicated deployment options?

1) BYOK import: do you support direct KMIP imports, envelope-wrapped key upload (customer-provided wrapping key), and/or remote EKM proxy integrations? Please outline the recommended flow for customers that cannot export plaintext key material from their HSM.

2) Key escrow / escrow alternatives: do you provide an optional escrow service, or do you offer a zero-escrow model with customer-managed key custody? What controls exist around escrow access and attestation?

3) HSM models and attestation: which HSM vendors/models are supported (on-prem connector and in-cloud HSMs)? Do you provide remote attestation artifacts (e.g., TPM/SGX quotes or signed HSM attestations)?

4) Rotation and re-encryption: recommended rotation cadence, handling of active KV caches, and rolling re-encryption strategy for persisted data and cached KV entries. How do you guarantee no downtime for inference during key rotation?

5) TLS profile: minimum TLS version, cipher suites for public hosted APIs vs private VPC endpoints, and guidance on mutual TLS between customer vaults and Redwood EKM gateway.

We'd like the answers in a concise technical note and any procedural runbook or diagram you can share. Ideally we can close these questions this week.

Appreciate it,
Jacob
Director, Information Security
Medicorp
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Jacob Liao <jacob.liao@medicorp.com>
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 5 Nov 2026 12:40:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Questions: BYOK/brokered escrow paths + TLS cipher profile

Jacob — thanks for the clear list. Long answer short: we support multiple BYOK patterns (KMIP, envelope import, and an optional customer-managed EKM proxy), we do not require escrow but offer an auditable escrow option for customers who need it, and our TLS+mutual-TLS configurations are configurable per deployment. Below I summarized recommended flows and included links to the attached runbook and sequence diagram.

-- BYOK import patterns (recommended order) --
1) KMIP import (preferred when customer HSM supports KMIP import): customer exposes an import endpoint (short-lived cert) and Redwood's onboarding agent pushes an import wrapped per KMIP. Metadata and key versions are recorded.

2) Envelope-wrapped upload (common for air-gapped HSMs): customer encrypts the key under a wrapping KEK (RSA-OAEP or AES-KWP) and uploads the envelope via our private API and the onboarding agent. In this flow Redwood never receives plaintext key material; the agent performs local unwrap into the local HSM or passes a wrapped token to the EKM gateway.

3) EKM proxy (recommended when customer wants total custody): customer deploys a lightweight EKM proxy in their VPC that implements a narrow KMIP/REST shim. Redwood calls that proxy to perform cryptographic ops (sign/decrypt) without key export. This is effectively a remote KMS call pattern; we provide an open-source EKM proxy reference implementation and hardened connector.

-- Escrow options --
- Zero-escrow (default): customers can choose to retain exclusive custody; Redwood stores only wrapped key handles and rotated key identifiers. No plaintext is persisted in our control plane.
- Optional escrow: for customers that require an escrow record (legal/regulatory needs), we offer an auditable escrow vault backed by an HSM (FIPS 140-2 level 3 vetted models). Escrow access requires multi-party approval (three-person quorum) and is logged with attestation artifacts.

-- Supported HSMs and Attestation --
- In-cloud: AWS CloudHSM, Google Cloud HSM (where applicable), and Azure Dedicated HSM.
- On-prem / appliance: nCipher nShield Connect, Thales Luna (models LUNA SA series), and Fortanix Data Security Manager connectors.
- Attestation: we can produce signed module attestations and HSM serial-level evidence; for EKM proxy/agent-based flows we support TPM 2.0 quoting and can provide SGX enclave measurement for enclaves used in private deploys. For dedicated contracts we can share vendor-signed attestation bundles under NDA.

-- Rotation & re-encryption --
- Rotation cadence: default policy is 90 days for envelope KEKs; customer can set policies down to 30 days or up to annual depending on classification.
- Re-encryption strategy: when a key material is rotated, existing persisted artifacts are re-encrypted lazily on first access where possible, and proactively via a background rewrap job for bulk data. For inference KV caches (per-tenant KV caches) we maintain concurrent key versions in the runtime and do key id switching with a short overlap window (configurable, default 5 minutes) to avoid rejecting in-flight requests.
- No downtime guarantee: our runtime supports dual-key reads during the overlap and atomic update of key IDs, ensuring in-flight sessions continue to be served. We also provide a canary rollout path for key swaps.

-- TLS and Mutual TLS recommendations --
- Public hosted API: TLS 1.2 (minimum) and TLS 1.3 preferred; accepted suites prioritize ECDHE + AES-GCM or CHACHA20-POLY1305 (e.g., TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256, TLS_CHACHA20_POLY1305_SHA256).
- Private / VPC endpoints: TLS 1.3 recommended; we require mTLS for customer-managed EKM proxies and onboarding agents.
- Certificate management: support for ACME + private CA; OCSP stapling enabled on all endpoints. We recommend short-lived certs (7-30 days) for EKM proxies and rotate client certs with keystore rotation policies tied to KMS.

-- Audit & evidence --
- All KMS operations are logged to an immutable audit trail with HMAC-chained records and optional export to customer SIEM (syslog/Splunk/Datadog).
- For procurement we can provide a short package: runbook, sequence diagram, supported HSM models list, and a sample attestation bundle under NDA (attached).

I've attached: redwood_byo_runbook_v2.pdf (procedural steps), ekm-proxy-sequence-diagram.png (flow), and tls-cipher-matrix.csv (cipher mapping by endpoint).

If helpful, I can schedule a 30-minute walkthrough this week with Irene (integration lead) to show the EKM proxy reference and runtime key-overlap mechanics.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Head of Security Solutions
Redwood Inference

Thanks Rishi — this is very helpful and covers most of our asks. A couple quick clarifications:

> Envelope-wrapped upload (common for air-gapped HSMs): customer encrypts the key under a wrapping KEK (RSA-OAEP or AES-KWP) and uploads the envelope via our private API and the onboarding agent.

1) In that flow, who performs the unwrap? Our security team cannot allow Redwood-hosted agents to perform the private unwrap inside a Redwood-managed HSM unless we have explicit escrow/attestation. Is the intended pattern for the on-prem agent to perform unwrap and then call Redwood with a wrapped handle, or for Redwood to call back into a customer proxy?

2) For the EKM proxy: does Redwood sign the requests with its own client certificate or do you rely purely on mutual auth to the proxy? We need to understand the authentication real estate to put into our network firewall rules.

3) Can we get a short diagram that shows the zero-escrow agent flow vs the escrowed import flow (just a single-slide PNG) — that would help our architecture board.

If you can confirm those three items I think Procurement can move forward with the NDA and the technical review.

-jacob

Jacob — great questions, answers inline and next steps at the bottom.

> 1) Who performs the unwrap?
- For envelope upload the recommended pattern is the on-prem onboarding agent performs the unwrap locally into the customer HSM or local KMIP server. The agent then registers a wrapped handle (non-exportable token) with Redwood. If customers cannot run an agent, the alternative is the EKM proxy approach where Redwood calls the customer-managed proxy and cryptographic ops occur in the customer HSM (no plaintext leaves). We do not require Redwood-managed HSM to receive plaintext keys for private deployments by default.

> 2) Authentication to the EKM proxy
- We use mTLS mutual authentication for all EKM proxy calls. Redwood presents a client certificate (rotated regularly) and the proxy validates it. Optionally, we support bearer tokens signed with customer KMS-backed keys for an additional layer. For firewall rules we recommend allowing outbound TLS to the proxy's IP/DNS and pinning the client cert fingerprint if the proxy is reachable by DNS.

> 3) Diagram request
- Attached is a single-slide PNG showing zero-escrow agent flow vs escrowed import flow (ekm-proxy-sequence-diagram.png).

Next steps:
- I'll loop in Irene to set a 30-minute technical walkthrough. We can also provide a vendor-signed attestation bundle after NDA if Procurement needs it.
- If Procurement is ready I can open a DocuSign envelope for the NDA and a scoped SOC2 addendum specific to key custody. Link: https://www.docusign.com/recipient/REDACTED-Envelope-12345
